key_insight: A transversely isotropic model with a deformation-dependent semisoft modulus captures stiffness anisotropy and enables finite reorientation onset followed by a broad, flatter stress plateau.
engineering_relevance: The model supports direction-dependent mechanical predictions for main-chain liquid crystal elastomers under finite deformation.
method: Combine finite-strain, isothermal network elasticity with a deformation-dependent quadratic semisoft penalty.
Use a weak-fluctuation statistical closure to obtain exponential evolution from an initial to a residual semisoft modulus.
Derive perpendicular-tension relations linking rotating-stage stress to the semisoft modulus and its deformation derivative.
evidence_signal: Comparisons with orientation-dependent measurements using one common parameter set capture the principal stiffness contrast and broad perpendicular plateau.
watch_item: Discrepancies remain in oblique stresses and intermediate-angle initial moduli, limiting confidence for off-axis predictions.
paper_title: A transversely isotropic constitutive model for semisoft elasticity in main-chain liquid crystal elastomers
